findings.title: Flexbox on .small-action makes the action button's float ineffective
findings.body: Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` makes its children flex items, and `float` is ignored on flex items. The existing `button { float: right; }` at line 309 therefore no longer pushes the button to the right; because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`, the button will sit immediately after the description instead of at the far right. This is a layout regression for small-action rows such as post notices.

findings.title: align-items mixin does not cover the same legacy engines as flexbox mixin
findings.body: `@mixin flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, but `@mixin align-items()` never emits the matching legacy Mozilla property `-moz-box-align`. In engines that use the old Mozilla box model, the flex container is created but vertical alignment is ignored, so `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action` are not centered as intended. The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real IE property; the valid property is `-ms-flex-align` (already present). Add `-moz-box-align` or drop the `-moz-box` display, and remove the invalid `-ms-align-items`.

findings.title: order mixin maps 0-based order values directly to 1-based legacy ordinal groups
findings.body: The legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-based (default 1), while the modern `order` property is 0-based (default 0). `@mixin order($val)` passes `$val` unchanged to both families. The current callers use `order(2)` and `order(3)`, so relative ordering happens to work, but any future caller using `order(1)` — or relying on parity with the modern default — will get incorrect ordering in legacy engines. The legacy properties should use a 1-based value such as `$val + 1`, or the mixin should document/enforce the difference.
